verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own material says it converts Docker images to fast-booting VMs and runs them globally. `fly launch` creates, configures and deploys an app, `fly machine run` builds and starts a Machine in one line, and `fly doctor` checks Docker. One community user reported container pushes failing 70-80% of the time and another described stuck deploys; these point to reliability problems rather than a missing capability, so they lower confidence and quality but do not establish a dispute. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party Dockerfile/image deployment docs (the explicit Docker-image statement comes from a blog post), positive independent hands-on corroboration of reliable container deploys.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy applications packaged as Docker containers

citations.quote: Fly.io converts Docker images to fast-booting VMs and runs them globally.
Run `fly launch` from inside your project source directory to create, configure, and (for most apps) deploy a new application.
The `fly machine run` command is a tool to configure, build, and start a new Machine in one line.
